description:
ASTRA Mission Team is a student-led team exploring the future of lunar exploration through technology, creativity and innovation.

Our project, ASTRA — Space Exploration, Mission Command 3.2, is an educational lunar mission-management prototype designed to help students understand the challenges of managing a future Moon outpost.

Our goal is to make space exploration concepts more interactive and accessible through software and creative problem-solving.
summary:
ASTRA (Advanced Space Technology & Research Administration) is an educational lunar mission-management prototype designed to help students explore the challenges of operating a future Moon outpost.

The platform brings mission command, simulated resource management, fictional astronaut profiles, crew wellbeing check-ins, daily schedules, a 3D lunar base, an interactive mission assistant, NASA science resources and mission reporting into one workspace.

ASTRA helps students understand how decisions involving resources, crew coordination and mission planning affect an outpost. It combines interactive technology with space-science learning to make complex exploration concepts more accessible.

The project is an original student concept, developed with AI assistance in software design and coding.
details:
ASTRA — Space Exploration, Mission Command 3.2

Project overview

ASTRA is an educational lunar mission-management prototype inspired by the challenges of establishing and operating a future lunar outpost. It is designed to help students explore how astronauts and mission teams coordinate resources, schedules, crew responsibilities and scientific activities.

Main features

1. Command
A central mission overview displaying simulated mission conditions and resources.

2. 3D Base
A visual representation of a lunar outpost to help users explore the mission environment.

3. Crew
Fictional astronaut profiles and mission roles.

4. Wellbeing Lab
Non-medical crew check-ins designed to introduce the importance of astronaut wellbeing.

5. Daily Schedule
A five-sol timetable for organising activities during the lunar mission.

6. ASTRA Assistant
A rule-based assistant that explains mission concepts and helps users understand the platform.

7. NASA Science
NASA science resources and source links, with optional access to NASA data services when internet access and the relevant service are available.

8. Mission Report
Tools for reviewing and exporting mission information and reports.

9. Administrator Portal
A demonstration area for managing fictional crew, schedules, dataset records, announcements and demo permissions.

How ASTRA works

Users explore the mission dashboard, review the simulated situation, make decisions using the available controls, record mission activities and review the resulting information.

The project brings several aspects of mission management into one educational workspace, helping students understand how different decisions can affect a lunar outpost.

Data and limitations

ASTRA distinguishes simulated mission information from NASA information and resources. Its fictional crew and mission conditions are educational examples, not real astronaut or spacecraft data.

ASTRA is a prototype for learning and demonstration. It does not control spacecraft, provide medical services, or operate a real lunar base. Its administrator permissions are demonstration features rather than production-grade security.

Development and AI acknowledgement

The original ASTRA concept, project direction and feature requirements were provided by the student project founder. AI assistance was used during software design, coding and development.
